figure.title: Figure 6 (continued). (b) Drag coefficient. Aerodynamic characteristics of the 35 deg sweptback wing-body configuration: drag coefficient against lift coefficient, one polar per Mach number.
figure.x_axis: Lift coefficient, C_L, on staggered scales. Common axis used here = the M = 0.50 scale: left frame line = -0.2, grid every 0.1, right frame line = 3.0 (33 vertical lines). The label row under the plot reads -.2 at the left frame, then one '0' per Mach number every 0.2 (M = 0.50, .70, .85, .90, .925, .95, .975, 1.00, 1.02, 1.035, 1.085, 1.10, 1.13, each centred under its cell of the Mach-number box), then .2, .4, .6 at the right (M = 1.13 scale, .6 at the right frame). So CL = 0 of the M = 0.90 polar is the 4th '0', the common-axis line 0.6 (the line that ends at the top of the box under the '.90' cell).
figure.y_axis: Drag coefficient, C_D (grid 0 to 0.22 by 0.01; frame lines at 0 and 0.22)
figure.content_note: M = 0.90 polar: upright-triangle symbols (apex up), 10 symbols, faired curve through them. Most symbols hide the grid lines inside them (white-filled). Two places need judgement: at CL about 0.28 a right-pointing triangle of the M = 0.95 polar overlaps the M = 0.90 triangle and hides its centre dot (p3); at CL about 0.66 two M = 0.90 triangles overlap, offset 9 px vertically, both outlines and both dots visible but merged with each other's lines (p6, p7).
